newsitem.title: USA: Ashland to develop field offshore Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Ashland to develop field offshore Nigeria.

text.p: Ashland Inc said Thursday its affiliate, Ashland Nigeria Exploration Unlimited, has declared the Okwori South Field commercial and plans to proceed with its development pending approval by the Nigerian authorities.
Ashland said it expects oil will be flowing from the field by July 1998 at a daily production of more than 20,000 barrels a day.
The field, owned jointly by Ashland and Total SA, is located about 40 miles offshore, in water about 450 feet deep.

Ashland Exploration Inc spokesman Mark D. Pierce said the development decision follows the drilling of the Okwori South No. 3 well which found a combined 627 feet of hydrocarbon, of which up to 380 feet is oil, in a number of reservoirs.

Earlier, Ashland noted, it had drilled two other wells on the structure, which is located in Oil Prospecting License (OPL) 90. Okwori South No. 1 tested 6,184 barrels of oil per day from the Agbada formation. The No. 2 well encountered 297 feet of oil in a number of reservoirs.
The company said it is anticipated up to six subsea wells will be required to develop the field and a FPSO (Floating/Production/Storage/Offloading) vessel will be used as the production facility.
"Okwori is a very complex geologic structure, therefore additional drilling in untested fault blocks is anticipated," said W. Paul Tiefel, senior vice president of Ashland Exploration.
Once production starts, additional exploratory work likely will follow to further delineate Okwori and to explore other structures on the license, Ashland said.

This drilling is a part of a multiple well exploratory program under the 1992 Production Sharing Contract (PSC) between the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation and the joint venture of Ashland and Total.
Under the PSC, Ashland operates OPLs 90 and 225.
